label: late copy-phase step in long sequences, strongest when the fed-back input is i
explanation: Never fires during the original-input phase. Only active at the delimiter step (25% of mass) or in the copy phase (75%), and mostly in long sequences (L=9 holds 72% of mass, L>=8 holds 91%, nothing for L<=4). The strongest single cue is the copied input token i: copy steps where i is fed back hold 43% of mass (lift about 11x), and they make up most of the top activations. The rest of the activity is spread thinly over other copy steps and delimiter steps in L=9 sequences, with weak preferences for output tokens y/a/q. Recall position matters: it almost never fires at recall_idx 1-2, and the rate climbs toward the end of L=9 sequences. The predicate (copy phase, input i, L>=8) reaches dev precision 0.41, recall 0.26, mass recall 0.36. Broadening it to all delimiter/copy steps with L>=8 covers 91% of mass but has precision 0.04. Much of the activation is not captured by any simple token rule.
